title: Groupe de Galois motivique : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is the closing item (3°) of a two-page note headed 'Remarques sur la caractérisation des classes de coh. D.R. essentiellement algébriques, par bigraduation ou par réalité'.

Setting from the previous page:
- K ⊂ C is a subfield and M is a motive over K, with de Rham realization T_DR(M), a K-vector space.
- Algebraic classes are Hom(1,M) = M^G, the invariants under the motivic Galois group G. Their de Rham image is Hom(1,M)⊗_Q K ⊂ T_DR(M).
- Two necessary conditions are recorded:
  - a) Hodge condition: algebraic classes lie in the (0,0) part of the Hodge bigrading of T_DR(M)⊗_K C.
  - b) Reality condition: Hom(1,M)⊗_Q (K∩R) lies in the real structure (T_DR(M)_C)_R that comes from Betti cohomology.
- The question is whether a), b), or both characterize algebraic classes.

What the previous page establishes:
- 1°) If K = Q and G is not connected, a) and b) together cannot suffice. For finite G (Artin motives, weight 0), a) is empty, and b) amounts to the field L cut out by M being totally real. So one must restrict, e.g. to K = Q̄, and consider all embeddings K → C.
- 2°) The converse of a) alone is false even over Q̄. Take G of dimension ≥ 3. The bigrading is given by a cocharacter (j_1,j_2): G_m² → G' = Isom-twisted form of G (G' = ad(P), with P = Isom_⊗(T_B⊗K, T_DR)). If T is the image of that torus, choose a faithful representation V with V'^T ≠ V'^{G'}. Then there are (0,0) de Rham classes that are not motivic. This is the familiar observation that the Mumford–Tate group can be strictly smaller than the motivic Galois group if one only knows the Hodge torus.

This page, 3°): what remains is the possible converse to b) when K is algebraically closed. If K ≠ Q̄, one imposes the condition for all embeddings σ: K → C, possibly strengthened by a further condition c) (defined elsewhere, not on these two pages).

In modern terms the question is:
- Take a de Rham class over an algebraically closed K.
- Suppose that for every complex embedding of K it is real with respect to the Betti real structure (perhaps plus extra conditions).
- Is it then algebraic, i.e. motivic?

This is a reality-condition variant of what later became 'de Rham–Betti classes' and Deligne's 'absolute Hodge classes', where one demands a property for every embedding σ: K → C. It is posed, not answered.
errors: No outright error on this page; it only poses a question.
The precise content of condition c) is not on this page or the previous one, so the strengthening cannot be fully reconstructed.

As stated, b) is only a reality condition, which is much weaker than Betti rationality. Even over Q̄ a converse to b) alone looks implausible without strong extra hypotheses: the real subspace is large, and the condition 'K∩R' degenerates for algebraically closed K, whose image under σ need not meet R in a field over which things are defined. Hence the need for 'toutes les immersions' and a condition c).

ideas.what: Seek a characterization of algebraic (motivic) de Rham classes over an algebraically closed field K by imposing a reality/Betti condition for every embedding K → C
ideas.modern_name: absolute Hodge classes / de Rham–Betti classes; 'for all σ: K → C' condition
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (absolute Hodge cycles, 1979/1982); de Rham–Betti classes discussed by André (2004) in connection with the Grothendieck period conjecture
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck's period conjecture appears in a footnote of 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties' (1966); the 'all embeddings' formulation of 1965 is not, to my knowledge, in his published texts

ideas.what: Restricting to K algebraically closed (or Q̄) to avoid the counterexamples coming from non-connected motivic Galois groups (Artin motives)
ideas.modern_name: role of the connected component G^0 versus π_0(G) and Artin motives
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in Tannakian motive theory (Saavedra 1972; Deligne–Milne 1982)

missed.claim: In 1965 Grothendieck explicitly left open whether a reality (Betti-real) condition, imposed for all complex embeddings of an algebraically closed base field and possibly strengthened by a condition c), characterizes algebraic de Rham classes. This is an early 'for every embedding σ' formulation, foreshadowing absolute Hodge / de Rham–Betti classes.
missed.quote: Reste la question éventuelle d'une réciproque à b) si K alg. clos, en prenant (si K ≠ Q̄) toutes les immers. K → C, et en renforçant aussi au besoin avec la condition c).
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that the 'all embeddings' idea behind Deligne's absolute Hodge classes was already in Grothendieck's motivic Galois group notes in 1965. Mathematically, the real-structure variant is weaker than the de Rham–Betti rationality studied by André and others; it is historically interesting but not a new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a single open question. It interestingly anticipates the 'for all embeddings σ: K → C' philosophy of absolute Hodge cycles and de Rham–Betti classes, but Grothendieck's 1960s motivic and period ideas are broadly known, and nothing is proved here.
transcription_corrections: The small circled insertion above 'question' is hard to read; it may be 'au moins' rather than 'éventuelle'.
'renforçant' is plausible but uncertain; the scrawl could also be another participle such as 'complétant'.
The closing symbol may be 'c)' or another letter; the text reads 'avec la condition c)'.
